result.topic_en: Riemann studies when the theta function vanishes, describing the zero set of θ(v_1,…,v_p) as the set of v congruent to sums −Σ_1^{p−1} α^{(ν)} taken over p−1 arbitrary points; he notes that θ is even and derives that the 2p−2 zero points form the zeros of a differential of the first kind.

methods.what: Theta function vanishes at points congruent to minus a sum of p−1 Abel integrals
Converse: every zero of theta has this form (Riemann vanishing theorem)
Theta is even, by replacing summation indices m by −m in the series
The 2p−2 points have Abel sum ≡ 0; they are the zeros of a differential of the first kind (canonical divisor)
Zeros given as common roots of F=0 and a linear combination of the φ's
